runs.text: de manda em todo caſo, ou por todas as vias.

lines.note: Continues the preceding page's explanation of a demand: in any case, or by every means. The opening de belongs to running text, not a repeated catchword here.
Hitomoji is the onion-name glossed by Portuguese cebolla; the botanical meaning is supplied directly, without imposing a modern species identification.
Hitomomi denotes one forceful effort or rush. The divided Fito- begins the example on the next physical line. Enlargement and comparison with impeto below support a damaged t rather than OCR impero.

Fito- plus momi forms hitomomi; shiro wo semuru means attacking a fortress. The intervening mǒde remains provisional rather than being replaced with an expected construction. The OCR's leading l is extraneous ink, not part of momi.

runs.text: a fortaleza de hum impeto, ou furia.

lines.note: Completes combater: assaulting the fortress in one rush or fury. This supports the military interpretation of shiro wo semuru above.
Hitomuki and hitomukini denote intense, single-minded application. Latin l introduces the alternative; Adu. identifies the adverb, whose Portuguese gloss continues as intensamente.

runs.text: mente, ou com todas as forças, & cuidado.

lines.note: Completes intensamente and explains it as using all one's strength and care, not merely facing in one physical direction.
Hitomukini mono wo suru is doing something with complete application. Fazer al- starts the Portuguese translation across the line break.
Completes alguma cousa desta maneira; the next example begins hitomukina, an adjectival form modifying hito on the following row.
Hito completes the Japanese phrase for a determined person; the Portuguese relative clause continues below and specifies wholehearted application.

runs.text: grande aplicação ſe emprega em algũa couſa.

lines.note: Completes the portrait of a determined person who devotes himself to something with great application. The scan supports aplicação, not the OCR's aplicoção.
Hitomurasame is one passing shower; the Portuguese explains a burst of rain. Enlargement supports chuua, retaining the historical u/v spelling rather than OCR chaua or modern chuva.
The water passes quickly: this completes the short-shower definition, not a separate Japanese entry. Agoa is retained as the printed historical spelling.

Hitonami and hitonamini describe being together with others or in common. The small article os is damaged on its right side; the residual rounded shape and following outros support os rather than OCR cs.
Outros completes the preceding phrase, and em commum supplies the second gloss. The meaning is collective or shared rather than the modern evaluative sense of ordinary ability.
Hitonayami is trouble or torment caused to someone. The al- at the end belongs to Portuguese alguem on the next row.
Hitonayamini naru koto wo suru means doing something that causes another person distress. The example's final suru is divided at the physical line break.
Ru completes suru; the translation describes acts that mortify or give pain. Its relative clause continues onto the next line.
Pena aos outros completes the translation as pain inflicted on others. The short row is real body text and must not be absorbed into the following headword.
Hitokiwa means notably or to a marked degree, matching grandemente. The headword and example both support Fitoqiua rather than OCR Fituqiua; the example continues with sei wo iruru below.
Sei wo iruru means putting effort into something. With hitokiwa, it matches the Portuguese expression for outstanding diligence rather than a literal insertion.
Gencia completes dili-gencia, the Portuguese noun for diligence. The small c is not an o: OCR genoia would destroy the word.

runs.text: O fazer, ou ſer como homem nas

lines.note: Hitorashii is behaving as a proper person in manners and refinement. The gloss is evaluative, not a claim that the person merely resembles a human physically.
Cortesias and primor complete the social-manners gloss. The visible i in corteſias replaces OCR t; Fitoraxij begins the illustrative adjectival phrase.
Hito completes hitorashii hito; Idem sends the reader back to the same meaning. This two-word fragment is not an independent headword.
Hitorigo is an only child, directly matched by filho unico. No missing extra syllable needs to be supplied from the modern hitorikko form.
Hitorigoto is talking to oneself. The following example repeats the stem clearly, and the damaged headword supports goto rather than the OCR's j oto.
Hitorigoto wo yuu, alternatively suru, means speaking to oneself. The Latin alternative marker l is not part of the Japanese phrase.
The Portuguese specifies muttering between one's teeth. This is an explanatory nuance of the preceding Japanese example, not a new lexical entry.

Hitorimi here describes an unsupported person. The headword is heavily abraded; enlargement, the gloss, and the subsequently consulted NINJAL index support Fitorimi rather than OCR Frorimi. Deſemparada retains the historical vowel rather than modern desamparada.
Completes the unsupported-person gloss: lacking another who can help him. The verb is socorra, with a long initial s in the scan, not OCR jocorra.

Hitorimushi is an insect attracted to lamplight, compared with a butterfly. Enlargement supports Bichinho through the surviving ch and inho; the capital is badly abraded, so the reading also relies on the insect context.
Ao derredor da candea describes circling the lamp. The contiguous derredor is visible; OCR dea redor introduced a spurious vowel and boundary.

runs.text: Homem que eſtà ſò, ou paſſa, &

lines.note: Hitoriudo denotes a person alone. The Portuguese covers both being alone and passing one's life alone; the latter construction continues below.
Vive so completes the preceding coordinated verbs. It is a genuine short continuation, not a page-end remnant.

runs.text: O dedo com que moſtramos, ou

lines.note: Hitosashiyubi is the pointing finger. The Portuguese describes its function rather than using a Latin anatomical name.
Apontamos em alguem completes the pointing-finger description. The object is a person being pointed out, not another headword.
Hitosugini first means straight or rightly, hence Rectamente, and then single-mindedly or intensely. The c/t sequence corrects OCR Rebtamente without changing the historical gloss.

runs.text: te ſem deſuiar, ou deuirtir noutra couſa. Vt,

lines.note: Completes intensamente: without deviating or diverting oneself to another matter. Vt introduces the religious example on the next row.

Hitosugini gose bodai no tsutome wo itonamu describes single-minded practice for enlightenment in the next life. The scan supports tçutomeuo, with the object particle uo, rather than OCR tçutomiguo. The apparent accent in OCR Fitôſugini belongs to the damaged letter area, not a secure long-o mark.

runs.text: Darſe às couſas da ſaluação intenſa-

lines.note: Mu completes itonamu. The Portuguese renders the Buddhist practice as devotion to the things of salvation; ſaluação is supported by the scan, not OCR ſalueção.
Mente completes intensamente, describing the manner of religious application. It remains its own physical line despite its brevity.
Hitotsuba is simply identified as an herb of that name. The damaged vowel in chamada is a, not OCR u; the definition alone does not establish a precise botanical species.

runs.text: Ponte feita de hum ſoo pao.

lines.note: Hitotsubashi is a bridge made from a single piece of wood. The weak b in the headword belongs to baxi, not the OCR's separated i axi.
Hitotsugaki denotes separately listed written items or memoranda. The Portuguese word escrito is divided across this line and the next.

Each written item is separate in itself. The example continues into gaki wo suru below. Enlarged reinspection leaves the internal t of expected Fitotçu unestablished; the visible Fito çu is retained with this warning rather than silently supplying the lost type.
Gaki wo suru completes the example of making itemized notes. Suru, supported by the visible final u and the Portuguese infinitive fazer, replaces OCR sura.

runs.text: Modo de tingir com certas liſtras

lines.note: Hitotsumaze names a dyeing arrangement with contrasting stripes. Tingir and certas liſtras, visible despite abrasion, correct OCR ingir and cestas liſia; the following rows explain the colour contrast.

runs.text: ou cores hũas mais intenſas que outras. ¶

lines.note: Some colours are more intense than others. The damaged right-end fragment starts the repeated hitotsumaze example; Fi is linguistically expected before totçumaje below, but the i and terminal mark remain weak even at enlargement. The OCR fragment remains provisional, as does the abraded comparative qu outres.
The divided headword forms hitotsumaze no kosode, a silk garment in that dyeing style. Veſtido de ſeda com is supported by the scan rather than OCR Veſtdo and con-.
These stripes or colours complete the description of the kosode. The Portuguese line supplies the referent of the dyeing term, not another Japanese synonym.

Hitotsu no hoshi is equated with hokuto and glossed as the northern star. Preserve the dictionary's equivalence rather than imposing a modern astronomical distinction between the pole star and the Northern Dipper.
Hitotegiwa denotes a notable or masterly accomplishment, with emphasis on finish. The gloss continues its assessment on the next line.
Hitotegiwa shita is the past-tense example: he performed a notable feat. The scan supports xita, not OCR xia, and acabada rather than arabada.

runs.text: hũa façanha, ou hua obra prima, & bem

lines.note: Fez from the preceding row governs a feat or a masterly work. The second hua is retained without supplying an unprinted tilde merely for consistency.
Acabada completes bem acabada, describing the work as well finished; this short continuation remains a separate physical row.

runs.text: Fitoto xite. i, Fitoto yǔ mono.

lines.note: Hito to shite is explained by hito to yuu mono: one who is human, or as a human being. The explanatory i is editorial, not Japanese.
Homem and sendo homem complete the two Portuguese paraphrases of the preceding construction. Their contrast is nominal versus circumstantial, not two new senses of hito.

runs.text: Couſa igual, vniforme, ou da meſma

lines.note: Hitoshii means equal or alike, matching igual and uniforme. The Portuguese final da mesma continues into maneira below.
Ware to hitoshii mono means a person like me. The Portuguese Ho- begins homem on the next physical row.

runs.text: mem como eu, ou ſemelhante a mim.

lines.note: A man like me or resembling me completes ware to hitoshii mono. The paired corrections ſemelhante and mim restore words supported by the scan and its first-person comparison.
Hitoshio means markedly or particularly. NINJAL prompted a second look at the ending: the upright u supports Fitoxiuo. Both OCR Ficoxito and the initial visual Fitoxito failed to recover it.
Hitozure is human company or companionship. The example's repeated fitozzure supports the abraded headword; Aru- starts arukoozuru across the line boundary.
Arukoozuru tame ni hitozure ga nai means having no companion when intending to go walking. The prospective form belongs to historical Japanese morphology, not a corrupt modern aruku.

runs.text: fora, ou caminhar, não ter companhia. B.

lines.note: Fora completes ir fora, going out; the rest reiterates walking without company. B is the usage label at the end, visibly upright rather than part of the italic explanation.
Hitozute means conveying something through a third person. Recado por terceira peßoa provides the precise intermediary sense.

Hitozute ni moosumajii koto ja to yuute means saying it is not something to convey by messenger. The negative modal majii belongs with moosu; the scan does not support the OCR's internal space in mǒſuma jij.
Feiq. cites the Heike source, with Lib. 1 giving its book number. The Portuguese begins 'saying that it was', continuing into the reported prohibition below.

runs.text: couſa que naõ auia de dizer por recado.

lines.note: Completes the quotation's meaning: something that was not to be said through a message. Keep the printed carrier of the tilde in naõ rather than normalizing it to modern não.
Hitoe denotes something single or unlined. The following bag and garment examples make the material sense explicit.
Hitoe bukuro is an unlined bag, hence saco sem forro. The damaged c is not t; Sato is an OCR error rather than a Portuguese variant relevant here.

runs.text: Couſa ſingella, ou que naõ he dobra-

lines.note: Hitoena modifies something single, not doubled. Naõ supplies the necessary negative and is compatible with the damaged initial letter, unlike OCR raõ.

Da completes dobrada; the figurative gloss then describes a straightforward person. The compressed permet. is the printed metonymic/metaphorical explanation marker and should not be expanded in the transcription.
Sem refolho literally evokes absence of a fold and figuratively a lack of concealment or duplicity. It completes the characterization of the person above.
Hitoeni is first glossed singellamente, singly. The visible g corrects OCR Sinellamente; the example begins on this row and continues below.
Hitoeni mono wo kiru is wearing a single layer or kind of clothing. The Portuguese vestimenta phrase is completed on the next physical line.

runs.text: veſtido. ¶ Item, Em todo caſo. Vt,

lines.note: After completing vestido, the entry gives hitoeni the emphatic sense 'in any case'. The new example's hitoye- is the same stem, not OCR fitaye-.
Ni tanomu completes hitoeni tanomu, an earnest request. Portuguese peço vos encarecidamente explains the pragmatic force rather than a literal dependence alone.
Por todas as vias reinforces the earnest-request sense. This continuation belongs with tanomu, not with the next noun hitoyoo.
Hitoyoo denotes a useful service, task, or need. The visible circumflex is retained; the gloss's list continues below.

runs.text: proueitoſa que hum faz a alguem. ¶

lines.note: The useful action is something done for another person. Fito- begins the example hitoyoo ni tatsu on the following row.
Hitoyoo ni tatsu means being useful for such a service. The Portuguese permits either performing it or being fit to perform it, completed below.
Completes the service gloss: doing the work or being useful for doing it. The close of this entry is distinct from the following forceful-action verbs.
Hittakuri, hittakuru, hittakutta means snatching or seizing. The principal-part ending utta has two t strokes; OCR ueta would give an implausible inflection and is not supported by the crop.
Por força completes tomar, specifying seizure by force. It is not a second verb or a separate entry.
Hittate, hittateru, hittateta means lifting or pulling something up. The Portuguese begins with levantar an object and continues with the manner of grasping it.

runs.text: tomandoa com amaõ como armas, veſtido

lines.note: The object is taken in the hand, with weapons and clothing as examples. The printed amaõ spacing and tilde placement are retained rather than regularized.
Hito wo hittatsuru illustrates pulling a person up or along. The tsuru ending is a historical form corresponding to the headword's teru, not necessarily a mistaken extra consonant.

runs.text: por algue aleuantalo, ou leualo conſigo.

lines.note: Completes puxando: raise someone or take him along. The visible endings support aleuantalo and conſigo rather than OCR aleuantals and conſizo; the weak algue remains unexpanded.
Hittaoshi, hittao(su), hitta(oita) describes pulling someone or something down. The supplied oita principal part is retained as the historical inflection, not modernized to oshita.
Hittsukamaye means grasping forcefully, directly matched by afferrar com força. The printed maye sequence is part of the historical form.
Hittsuke is holding something firmly attached or seized. Ter afferrado is the Portuguese construction; OCR Tor affer ado loses the verb vowel and consonants.

Nusubito no kashira wo ba shujin begins an example concerning a lord and the chief of the thieves. Enlarged reinspection leaves the u and the gap in xu jin abraded; retain the provisional spaced reading rather than treating it as two Japanese words in interpretation.

Hittsukete completes the Japanese example. The Portuguese says the lord held firmly with him; it continues across the page. OCR fiut, uqete breaks a coherent verb into noise, while conſigo retains its visible long s.
Anticipates a cabeça do ladrão at the opening of f202. Retained as page furniture under the original stable ID, not counted twice in the running text. The terminal mark is faint.
